theorem_title: Source-band construction is bounded by encoder count
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.SourceBandCosts.time_le_encoderCount {N n p U D : ℕ} (hN : N ≤ n) :
    _root_.ThreeSum.LightSourceBandSetup.time N (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.BandScales.bandSize n) p
      (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.BlockSourceEncoding.modulus (_root_.ThreeSum.Scales.microHalf (_root_.ThreeSum.Scales.inputBits n)) (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.Scales.blockCount (_root_.ThreeSum.Scales.inputBits n))) U D ≤
      (1016*(Nat.log 2 (U+1)+Nat.log 2 (p+D+1)+1)+1946)*_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.StageBounds.encoderCount n+560 := by sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $N,n,p,U,D\in\mathbb N$ with $N\le n$. For the executable band width and global modulus at size $n$, the source-band setup time is at most $$\bigl(1016(\lfloor\log_2(U+1)\rfloor+\lfloor\log_2(p+D+1)\rfloor+1)+1946\bigr)\operatorname{encoderCount}(n)+560.$$

Retains all residue, histogram, and bucket construction charges in a uniform original-size bound. This supports the complete deterministic integer 3SUM runtime proof.
